correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the stratification for p≥5 over the finite field and its algebraic closure. For a unit coefficient, nilpotence is equivalent to 1 lying in the image (the kernel is one-dimensional), or equivalently f⁻¹ having no t^(p−1) term. For the converse choose the antiderivative with zero constant term; its nonzero linear term then gives a valid change of coordinate in the local algebra. Unit centralizers are scalar lines by the quotient rule. Linear-order coefficients are not nilpotent; order ≥2 raises the degree filtration. At minimal nonlinear order k≤h, the first possible term of fg′−gf′ has coefficient (ℓ−k)f_k g_ℓ, forcing proportionality modulo t^(p−k+1). Each normalized truncated direction has p−2k free coefficients; for each such direction the m entries have k coordinates each and at least one leading scalar must be nonzero. The order ≥h+1 locus is abelian by degree. These disjoint strata give the stated sum. Over the closure the low strata have affine parameters with a nonzero scalar vector, giving dimensions p−2k+mk; the unit stratum has dimension p−2+m and the high one mh. Pivot charts recover the normalized direction regularly. The largest dimension is attained at k=h and exceeds the unit dimension by (m−2)(h−1). The finite checker was inspected, not rerun; its only in-domain exhaustive field is F_5, and it does not check the geometric dimension.

originality.rationale: An earlier explicit all-q, all-m restricted count was not established. The exact count and dimension nevertheless follow mechanically from the known nilpotent-cone strata and centralizer formulas: choose the first entry of minimal order and then count earlier coordinates in the tail and later coordinates in that abelian centralizer. This is stronger prior coverage than just knowing the m=2 dimension. The inaccessible 2015 higher-tuple paper is not the basis of the decision.
residual_risks: The 2015 higher-arity theorem was not inspected in full text; whether it states the dimension in the frozen form is unresolved. Explicit priority for the arithmetic polynomial is also unresolved. The exact prior-implication check does not depend on either priority question.
